meta.title: Bounded, thread-safe resolver cache
meta.head: lru-cache
meta.pr: Bound the resolver cache (LRU) and make it thread-safe

C1.label: verified
C1.claim: `LruCache` keeps a `std::list` ordered from most to least recently used, and a `std::unordered_map` from each key to its place in the list.

C2.label: verified
C2.claim: The constructor throws `std::invalid_argument` when the capacity is 0.

C3.label: verified
C3.claim: `get` returns `std::nullopt` for a missing key; on a hit it moves the entry to the front of the list and returns a copy of the value.

C4.label: verified
C4.claim: `put` on an existing key replaces the value and moves the entry to the front; on a new key it adds the entry at the front and, when the size passes `capacity_`, erases the last entry from both the list and the map.

C5.label: inferred
C5.claim: Every public operation holds the `std::mutex` for its whole body, so threads can share one cache without corrupting the list or the map.
C5.why: get and put each start with a lock_guard (lines 19 and 27) that lives until the function returns, and there is a single mutex member (line 47) guarding both containers.

C6.label: verified
C6.claim: `Resolver::resolve` returns the cached address when `get` finds one; otherwise it calls `lookup` and stores the result with `put`.

C7.label: inferred
C7.claim: Two threads that miss on the same host at the same moment both call `lookup` and both store the answer: the cache stays correct, but the lookup runs twice.
C7.why: get, lookup and put are three separate steps (lines 8 to 10) and no lock spans them; each cache call takes and releases the mutex on its own.

C8.label: verified
C8.claim: `Resolver` gets a constructor that takes a capacity (default 128) and now holds an `LruCache` instead of a `std::map`.

C9.label: inferred
C9.claim: `LruCache` holds a `std::mutex`, which cannot be copied, so `Resolver` can no longer be copied; the `std::map` it held before could be.
C9.why: A class with a non-copyable member has a deleted copy constructor, and Resolver now contains one through its LruCache member. Code that copied a Resolver would stop compiling; nothing in the diff does so.

C10.label: unverified
C10.claim: Whether 128 hosts is a sensible default for the real workload is not shown anywhere in the diff.

C11.label: verified
C11.claim: The new test fills a cache of 2 entries, reads "a", adds "c" and checks that "b" was evicted and "c" is present, then checks that capacity 0 throws.

C12.label: inferred
C12.claim: No test covers the resolver using the cache, replacing a value for an existing key, or two threads sharing one cache.
C12.why: The only test builds an LruCache directly; it never calls put twice on the same key and starts no thread. The resolver has no test in the diff.

C13.label: verified
C13.claim: CMake gains a test target `lru_test` built from the new test file and registered with `add_test`.

C14.label: verified
C14.claim: src/main.cpp is reformatted only: the one-line `main` becomes several lines and a blank line follows the include; the tokens are unchanged.

C15.label: stated
C15.claim: The PR title says the cache is bounded and thread-safe. Bounded: yes, by its capacity. Thread-safe: each cache call is locked, but the resolver's get, lookup and put are separate steps, so two threads can repeat a lookup.

components.name: LRU cache
components.desc: A bounded, mutex-guarded cache that drops the least recently used entry.

components.name: resolver
components.desc: The resolver swaps its unbounded map for the cache; get, lookup and put are not atomic.

components.name: tests and build
components.desc: One test for the cache and a CMake target for it.

change.purpose: Stop the resolver cache from growing without limit: replace the plain map with a mutex-guarded LRU cache of fixed capacity.

cohorts.name: Bound and share the resolver cache
cohorts.why: One purpose: the cache has a fixed size and can be used from several threads.

cohorts.name: Formatting only
cohorts.why: No behaviour change; folded by default.

Y1.title: The LRU cache
Y1.order: Read first: the resolver is built on it.
Y1.sum: A template cache of fixed capacity that evicts the least recently used entry, with one lock around every call.

Y2.title: The resolver uses it
Y2.order: Second: composes layer 1. This is where the purpose lives.
Y2.sum: The resolver takes a capacity and holds the cache; resolve is get, lookup, put, with no lock across the three.
